headline: Q2 issuance surge masked a 1% Q3 revenue slowdown; operating margin stayed above baseline, but total debt rose above $7.35bn by 30 September 2026.
summary: Across the first three quarters of FY2026, revenue grew 7.9% year on year (illustrative, summed from the three 10-Qs) [2]. Growth was uneven: +8% in Q1, +15% in Q2 on MIS issuance, and +1% in Q3, when leveraged-finance issuance fell [2]. Nine-month operating margin was about 45.7% against 44.3% a year earlier (illustrative, summed from 10-Q operating income), so the T1 margin signpost is met year to date [2][4]. Q3 operating margin nonetheless fell 90 bps to 44.8% as operating and SG&A expense grew 2% against 1% revenue growth [2]. Total debt was $7,492 million at 30 September 2026, above the $7,351 million FY2025 level, which breaches the T3 invalidation threshold at quarter end [3][4]. Adjusted diluted EPS was $4.33, $4.68 and $4.14 in the three quarters, with Q1 and Q2 beating consensus and Q3 missing by 2.5% [2][3]. Consensus FY2026 EPS is $16.76, and the reverse DCF still requires 18.1% annual growth against 6.5% consensus revenue growth [3]. The earnings releases for these quarters were not available, so all quarterly figures come from the 10-Qs [1][2].
results_commentary:
Q3 FY2026 was the weakest quarter. Revenue rose 1% to $2,023 million (organic constant currency +3%) [2]. MIS external revenue fell 1% to $1,087 million because leveraged-finance issuance dropped against a strong prior-year quarter and higher market volatility. Investment-grade issuance tied to AI financing and Project and Infrastructure Finance activity partly offset this [2]. Operating and SG&A expenses rose 2%, driven by technology and AI usage costs and higher incentive compensation, so operating margin fell 90 bps to 44.8% and adjusted operating margin fell 30 bps [2]. Restructuring rose 29% to $27 million [2]. Reported diluted EPS of $4.24 (+18%) includes a $115 million divestiture gain. Adjusted diluted EPS of $4.14 (+6%) was below the $4.25 consensus, a 2.5% miss [2][3]. A lower share count (diluted shares down 4% to 173.3 million) supplied most of the EPS growth [2].

Q2 FY2026 was the strongest quarter. Revenue rose 15% to $2,185 million (organic constant currency +16%) [2]. MIS revenue grew 25% to $1,260 million on U.S. leveraged-finance issuance, investment-grade issuance from hyperscalers and data-center project finance. MA grew 4% to $925 million, held back by the MA Learning Solutions and MA Regulatory Solutions divestitures [2]. Operating and SG&A expenses rose 5%, so operating margin rose 480 bps to 47.9%. Part of this gain reflects higher incentive compensation, which rose with performance against targets [2]. Adjusted diluted EPS was $4.68, +31%, and beat the $4.25 consensus by 10% [2][3]. The GAAP EPS of $5.03 includes a $181 million gain on the divestiture of MA Regulatory Solutions [2].

Q1 FY2026 was steady rather than strong. Revenue rose 8% to $2,079 million, with MA and MIS each up 8% and organic constant currency growth of 6% [2]. Operating margin rose 30 bps to 44.3%, and adjusted operating margin rose 150 bps to 53.2% [2]. Costs grew as fast as revenue: operating and SG&A expenses rose 8%, from foreign exchange (2% unfavourable on operating expense, 3% on SG&A), salary increases and acquired headcount. A reserve for an international non-income tax obligation also sat in SG&A and offset part of the margin gain [2]. Adjusted diluted EPS was $4.33, +13%, and beat the $4.22 consensus by 2.6% [2][3]. Across the three quarters, restructuring charges totalled $86 million against $81 million a year earlier, with the Q2 and Q3 charges up year on year [2]. Restructuring was up in Q1 and Q3 and down in Q2 on a y/y basis, so the decline is not established across the period.

thesis_check.thesis: T1: Operating leverage keeps margins expanding, because operating and SG&A cost growth stays well below revenue growth.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 operating margin above 43.4% in the FY2026 10-K (filed about February 2027). Invalidation: below 40.6%, or restructuring rising again without a matching margin gain.
thesis_check.evidence: Operating margin was 44.3% in Q1 (44.0% a year earlier), 47.9% in Q2 (43.1%) and 44.8% in Q3 (45.7%), so the nine-month margin of about 45.7% is above the 43.4% signpost (illustrative) [2][4]. In Q3 operating and SG&A expense grew 2% against 1% revenue growth, and restructuring rose 29% to $27 million, which is the invalidation pattern at quarter level [2].

thesis_check.thesis: T2: The share price assumes growth well above consensus, so at consensus growth the implied return falls short of the cost of capital.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 revenue growth of at least 9% in the FY2026 10-K (about February 2027). Invalidation: FY2026 revenue growth of 12% or more.
thesis_check.evidence: Revenue growth was 8% in Q1, 15% in Q2 and 1% in Q3, so nine-month growth is about 7.9% (illustrative) [2]. Reaching the 9% FY2026 signpost needs Q4 growth well above the Q3 pace of 1%, and the reverse DCF still implies 18.1% growth against 6.5% consensus [2][3]. The Q2 jump to 15% shows growth can spike, which is why Q2 is marked weakened for the thesis, but the Q3 reading points back toward the consensus path.

thesis_check.thesis: T3: Deleveraging continues, but payouts near 94% of free cash flow will limit further debt reduction.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 total debt below $7.35 billion, with buybacks plus dividends at or below free cash flow, in the FY2026 10-K. Invalidation: total debt above $7.35 billion, or payouts above free cash flow for a second consecutive year.
thesis_check.evidence: Net cash moved from -$4,903 million at FY2025 to -$5,803 million in Q1 and -$6,026 million in Q2, and total debt was $7,492 million at 30 September 2026 against $7,351 million at FY2025 [3][4]. Cash and short-term investments fell from $2,448 million to $1,510 million in Q1 [3]. Buyback and dividend amounts for FY2026 are not in the 10-Q excerpts, so the payout test cannot be checked yet; the Q3 debt level already breaches the invalidation threshold [2][3].

thesis_check.thesis: T4: Debt-issuance cyclicality will show up in MIS earnings within a year, so the stock is exposed to a weaker issuance cycle.
thesis_check.signpost: Corporate Finance (CFG) revenue growth of at least 5% in FY2026, against 9% in FY2025, reported in the FY2026 10-K. Invalidation: CFG revenue growth at or above 9% in FY2026 even if debt issuance is flat. CFG is not reported separately in the 10-Q excerpts, so MIS external revenue is used as the proxy.
thesis_check.evidence: MIS external revenue grew 8% in Q1, 25% in Q2 on leveraged-finance and investment-grade issuance, and fell 1% in Q3 as leveraged-finance issuance dropped [2]. The swing from +25% to -1% within two quarters shows the issuance dependence the thesis describes. Adjusted diluted EPS of $4.14 in Q3 missed the $4.25 consensus by 2.5%; the $4.14 is the adjusted figure, while GAAP diluted EPS was $4.24 [2][3].

risk_update: Issuance cyclicality materialised in Q3 FY2026: MIS external revenue fell 1% as leveraged-finance issuance weakened, after a 25% rise in Q2 [2]. Cost risk from AI and technology spending also became visible: Q3 operating and SG&A expense growth of 2% was attributed partly to AI usage costs [2]. Regulatory and tax exposure is new in the period: Q1 included a reserve for an international non-income tax obligation, with interest and penalties recorded in non-operating expense [2]. Restructuring charges were $86 million across the first three quarters against $81 million a year earlier, so the cost programme has not yet reduced charges [2]. Two MA divestitures (MA Learning Solutions and MA Regulatory Solutions) lower reported MA revenue and headcount [2]. The filing says there are no material changes to the FY2025 risk factors [2]. The goodwill qualitative test at 31 July 2026 found no reporting unit more likely than not impaired, which eases the MA impairment risk for now [2].
outlook: The provided releases contain no FY2026 company guidance, and none is stated here. Consensus expects FY2026 revenue of $8,218.3 million (+6.5%) and EPS of $16.76, with FY2027 EPS of $18.59 [3]. The 90-day EPS revisions are -1.3% for FY2026 and -1.7% for FY2027, and the 30-day revision count was 1 of 23 for FY2026 [3]. Nine-month revenue growth of about 7.9% (illustrative) sits below the 9% T2 signpost, and Q4 would need to accelerate sharply from Q3's 1% pace to reach it [2][4]. Watch Q4 issuance volumes, the FY2026 operating margin against 43.4%, and whether total debt falls back below $7.35 billion in the FY2026 10-K [4].
